page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the n1-standard-8 sits primarily in the lower tiers for raw compute and memory throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench scores reflect weak to poor performance in single-core and multi-core operations, with text processing and compression tasks scoring in the bottom 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks remains average, with read speeds of 45.37 GB/sec and write speeds of 34.65 GB/sec. Ray tracing and small-model LLM text generation also achieve average performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource allocation profile without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. Because it lacks bundled local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, it is best suited for workloads that do not require high-speed local I/O or hardware acceleration. Appropriate workloads include standard web serving, basic database operations, and general-purpose applications that benefit from dedicated vCPUs but do not demand high-frequency single-core processing.
